p01.why: R has a member begin but no member end, so the loop uses the free begin and end that argument-dependent lookup finds in the global namespace.

p02.why: Newer compilers keep make()'s result alive until the loop ends, so main returns 0; GCC 14 and Clang 18 destroy it before the body, so main returns 1 (Q-0020).

p03.why: items in the range expression names the global array because the loop variable is not yet in scope there, so the sum is 6.

p04.why: Argument-dependent lookup finds lib::begin and lib::end, so the sum is 7 + 8.

p05.why: Only begin is a member, so both must be free functions, and no free begin exists.

p06.why: extern on the loop variable is rejected by GCC 16, Clang, and EDG; the Evidence says GCC 14 accepts a storage class there (Q-0026).

p07.why: static on the loop variable is rejected by GCC 16, Clang, and EDG, and GCC 14 accepts it (Q-0026).

p08.why: The range binds to an auto&& reference without a move and begin and end are called on it as an lvalue, so sum is 3 and named.data[1] becomes 20.

p09.why: An initializer statement can declare the array before the loop variable, and the sum is 3.

p10.why: thread_local on the loop variable is rejected by GCC 16, Clang, and EDG; the Evidence says GCC 14 accepts a storage class there (Q-0026).

p11.why: end is called one time while size is 2, so growing size in the body does not add iterations and seen is 2.

p12.why: The range has an incomplete type, an array of unknown bound of an incomplete class.

p13.why: The prvalue from make() lives for the loop, and the member begin and end give 1, 2, 3.

p14.why: An empty statement is a valid initializer statement before the loop variable.

p15.why: Both names are members, so the member form is used, and a data member begin of type int makes the loop invalid; the Evidence suggests EDG may instead use the free functions (Q-0098).

p16.why: Only begin is a member, so the loop uses the free r::begin and r::end, and the sum is 6.

p17.why: The braced list {1, 2.0} gives two different element types, so T cannot be deduced.

p18.why: A pointer is not an array, a braced list, or a class with begin and end, so it is not a range.

p19.why: The first loop sums 6 and the reference loop doubles each element, so a[2] is 6.

p20.why: The loop variable can be a structured binding, and 1*2 + 3*4 is 14.

p21.why: helpers::begin and helpers::end are visible only through the using-directive, and argument-dependent lookup on data::Bag does not find them.

p22.why: The loop's != comparison can come from operator==, and the iterator goes 0, 1, 2, so the sum is 3.

p23.why: The range expression is evaluated one time, so calls is 1 and n is 6.

p24.why: The outermost block of the body declares the loop variable v again.

p25.why: Clang and GCC call the callable data members begin and end and get 6, so main returns 0; EDG uses the member form only for member functions, finds no free begin or end, and likely rejects (Q-0098).

p26.why: begin and end can return different types, the loop compares with != against Stop, and the sum is 0 + 1 + 2.

p27.why: The member begin and end give 4, 5, 6.

p28.why: The braced list becomes a std::initializer_list<int> that the program declared first, and the sum is 6.

p29.why: The iterator has only postfix ++, and the loop needs prefix ++.
